flower.intro: Flower is the dried, cured bud of the cannabis plant, sold by weight. Think of it in terms of the cultivar on the label, and the lab results behind it.
points: The cultivar name is on the label
Lab results are a QR code or link away

pre-rolls.intro: A pre-roll is ground flower rolled in a paper or a wrap before it reaches the shelf. Some come single, some in packs, and some are infused with extract, so read the label before you compare.

vapes.intro: A vape heats cannabis oil instead of burning plant material. It comes as a cartridge that needs a battery, or as an all-in-one with the battery built in.
points: Check that a cartridge fits your battery
The label names the type of extract

edibles.intro: Edibles are cannabis products you eat, like gummies, chocolates and baked goods. Your body handles them differently than anything you inhale and they take longer to show up, so the serving size on the label is the first thing to read.
points: Keep them locked up, away from food

concentrates.intro: Concentrates are extracts made from the plant, in forms like wax, shatter, live resin and rosin. The names tell you about texture and how the extract was made, so ask if you don't know the term.
points: Ask what gear a format needs
Start low and go slow applies here too

beverages.intro: Cannabis beverages are drinks infused with cannabis, like seltzers, tonics and teas. Anything you drink can take a while to show up, so pace it by the serving size on the label, not by how fast it goes down.
points: Store it locked up, away from regular drinks

wellness.intro: This shelf holds tinctures, topicals and CBD products. A tincture is a liquid extract measured out by the dropper, and a topical is a product you apply to the skin.
points: Tinctures are measured by the dropper
Health questions go to your provider

lifestyle.intro: Lifestyle is the part of the shop that isn't cannabis: glassware, merch, accessories and culture essentials. Think of it as what stays on your shelf long after the visit.
